checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: A browser dashboard receives one-way server updates and reconnects over ordinary HTTP infrastructure. Which protocol is the simpler fit?

options.label: WebSocket
options.verdict: WebSockets are the right tool when both sides need low-latency messages, but they add connection-state and reconnect complexity that this one-way stream does not require.

options.label: Server-Sent Events
options.verdict: SSE matches server-to-browser updates, works with the HTTP model, and provides browser reconnection behavior. It is text-oriented and one-way, which is acceptable for the stated workload.

defend.prompt: Which qualifications make the choice sound?

options.label: Use WebSockets if clients must send frequent live messages
Reconnects need resume or missed-event handling
SSE provides arbitrary binary frames in both directions

defend.explain: Protocol selection follows communication shape. Both SSE and WebSockets create long-lived connections that must be balanced and observed, and either system needs an application-level strategy for gaps after disconnects.

checkpoints.title: Network reasoning ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Reason from load-balancer layers and transport behavior.

rungs.q: Which load balancer can route by HTTP path or header?
rungs.note: An application-layer balancer understands HTTP semantics and can route /api differently from /images.

rungs.q: Which transport preserves message boundaries but does not guarantee delivery?
rungs.note: UDP sends independent datagrams without TCP's ordered, reliable byte stream.

rungs.q: What is the main latency benefit of connection pooling?
rungs.note: Pooling avoids repeatedly paying TCP and TLS setup and reduces ephemeral-port and server handshake pressure.

checkpoints.explain: Network choices span different layers: L4 balances connections, L7 understands application requests, transports define delivery behavior, and connection reuse removes avoidable setup from the hot path.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build a global dynamic-request path from user to a healthy application instance.
palette: New TCP Connection per DB Query
checkpoints.explain: Global routing brings the client to a nearby edge or region. The L7 balancer applies HTTP routing and selects a healthy application instance. The service reuses pooled connections to dependencies instead of paying a fresh transport and TLS handshake on every call.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: API p99 rises while handlers and the database remain fast. Which signal identifies the bottleneck?
checkpoints.explain: The service is repeatedly paying connection establishment rather than reusing a healthy pool. Enable and correctly size keep-alive and dependency connection pools, then monitor reuse, queueing, and idle expiry.

wrong.Handler CPU: Low handler CPU shows compute is not saturated and does not account for time spent before useful work.
wrong.Database Query: The database stays fast and steady; its query time is not driving the new p99.
wrong.Packet Loss: The tiny stable loss rate does not correlate with the large increase in setup time.
